claim: arch_edge_editor.md, "Idempotence": "A field with cardinality one — preq_id — is set by add and cleared by remove, and adding to it when it already holds a different target is a refusal naming the current target, not a silent overwrite: a required field of cardinality one is retargeted by removing and adding, so that the removal is visible." This asserts the remove-then-add sequence the conflict refusal's own fix names (cardinalityOneConflictRefusal, author/edge_editor.go) is a working retarget path.
authoritative_source: arch_obligation_reporter.md's "Refusal is the validator's predicate" runs SchemaChecker over the after-state and refuses any entry the before-state did not carry; its fix table's row "a required field absent" names the fix carried for exactly that refusal. preq_id is a required field on a module requirement (schema/defaultProfile.json), so RemoveEdge's clearEdgeField deletes the key entirely (by design, per arch_edge_editor.md's own clearEdgeField description) rather than leaving it empty.
evidence: I ran the sequence arch_edge_editor.md's Idempotence section and cardinalityOneConflictRefusal's fix both prescribe: `spex edge remove` on R1's preq_id, followed by `spex edge add` with the new target. The remove's after-state is missing the required preq_id key, so Report's SchemaChecker pass newly introduces `schema: missing required property 'preq_id'` and IDValidator's `id: requirement <id> missing preq_id` — both absent from the before-state — so RemoveEdge itself refuses and preq_id is never cleared. The add that would follow never runs, and even if RemoveEdge's schema check were bypassed, the add would still hit the same cardinality-one conflict against the untouched value. No sequence of `spex edge add`/`spex edge remove` calls can retarget a required cardinality-one field: clearing it is always refused by the schema check arch_obligation_reporter.md itself specifies, so arch_edge_editor.md's Idempotence claim describes a path that cannot execute. EdgeEditor's own four checks (target exists, field declared, type permitted, module-local) and the DAG/obligations handoff to Report are unaffected and are covered by test_node_editing.md's N9–N13, none of which exercises this retarget path — the defect is isolated to the one Idempotence sentence and the fix text it licenses, so the rest of this bead's contract is implementable and implemented as specified.
proposed_fix: Either (a) exempt a required cardinality-one field from SchemaChecker's refusal specifically for the interval between a remove and its intended follow-up add — which needs a mechanism arch_obligation_reporter.md does not have, since it validates each command's after-state independently and holds no memory of an in-flight retarget across two commands — or (b), simpler and consistent with the rest of the contract, drop the retarget claim from arch_edge_editor.md's Idempotence section and instead specify that a cardinality-one conflict is refused with no retarget path via this module: the operator edits the file by hand (or the fixture) to change a required cardinality-one field, the same as any other required-field change that isn't a pure edge add/remove.
